{{ElectionsWA}}
The '''2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington''' were held on November 5, 2024, to elect the ten [[U.S. representative]]s from the [[U.S. state|State]] of [[Washington state|Washington]], one from each of the state's 10 [[Washington's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections coincided with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], as well as [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various [[2024 United States elections|state and local elections]]. The primary elections took place on August 6, 2024 using a [[top-two primary]] system where candidates of all parties run against each other and the top two vote-getters advance to the general election.
{{toclimit|2}}

===Candidates===
====Advanced to general====

{{see also|Washington's 3rd congressional district}}
The incumbent was Democrat [[Marie Gluesenkamp Perez]], who flipped the district and was elected with 50.1% of the vote in 2022 in what was considered to be a major upset.<ref name="HPVT"/> This was a rematch of the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington#District 3|2022 election]]. Marie Perez was considered to be one of the most vulnerable Democratic Representatives in 2024 due to the district's partisan lean with most polling considering the election to be a toss-up. Perez ultimately won re-election, improving on her narrow victory from [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington|2 years earlier]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-11-05 |title=Washington Third Congressional District Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-washington-us-house-3.html |access-date=2025-02-13 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

President [[Donald Trump]] [[2024 United States presidential election in Washington (state)|won]] the district by 3.3% on the same ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kondik |first=Kyle |date=2025-01-16 |title=The 2024 Crossover House Seats: Overall Number Remains Low with Few Harris-District Republicans |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/the-2024-crossover-house-seats-overall-number-remains-low-with-few-harris-district-republicans/ |access-date=2025-02-13 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref>

The incumbent was Republican [[Dan Newhouse]], who was re-elected with 66.5% of the vote in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington#District 4|2022]].<ref name="HPVT"/>

====Advanced to general====
* [[Dan Newhouse]] (Republican), incumbent U.S. representative<ref name = asked/>

{{see also|Washington's 5th congressional district}}
The incumbent was Republican [[Cathy McMorris Rodgers]], who was re-elected with 59.1% of the vote in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington#District 5|2022]]. On February 8, 2024, McMorris Rodgers announced she would not seek re-election after serving 10 terms.<ref name = CMR/>

====Advanced to general====
* [[Michael Baumgartner]] (Republican), [[Spokane County, Washington|Spokane County]] Treasurer (2019–present), former [[Washington State Senate|state senator]] from the [[Washington's 6th legislative district|6th district]] (2011–2019), and runner-up for [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] in [[2012 United States Senate election in Washington|2012]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madsen |first=Sue Lani |date=2024-02-26 |title=Michael Baumgartner joins crowded field in 5th Congressional District race |url=https://www.thecentersquare.com/washington/article_6efa5a5a-d4ea-11ee-b2b8-076a975158de.html |access-date=2024-02-26 |website=The Center Square |language=en}}</ref>

{{see also|Washington's 6th congressional district}}
The incumbent was Democrat [[Derek Kilmer]], who was re-elected with 60.0% of the vote in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington#District 6|2022]].<ref name="HPVT"/> On November 9, 2023, he announced that he would not seek re-election in 2024 after serving 6 terms.<ref name=KilmerWA/>

===Candidates===
====Advanced to general====
* Melissa Chaudhry (Democratic), nonprofit grant writer<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greenstone |first1=Scott |title=Pro-Palestinian Democrat challenges longtime Seattle Congressman Adam Smith |url=https://www.kuow.org/stories/pro-palestinian-democrat-challenges-seattle-congressman-adam-smith |website=[[KUOW-FM|KUOW]] |date=August 12, 2024 |access-date=August 18, 2024 |archive-date=August 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240818012437/https://www.kuow.org/stories/pro-palestinian-democrat-challenges-seattle-congressman-adam-smith |url-status=live }}</ref>

* Mark Greene (Republican), paralegal, perennial candidate, and Democratic nominee for {{ushr|AK|AL}} in [[2000 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|2000]] and [[2002 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|2002]]<ref name=WA2024/>
* David Ishii (Bipartisan{{efn|name=party|Not an actual political party. In Washington, independent candidates are allowed to choose a ballot label.}}), retired postal worker and perennial candidate<ref name=WA2024/>

====Advanced to general====

* Kurtis Engle (Union{{efn|name=party}}), [[U.S. Navy]] veteran and candidate for secretary of state in [[2022 Washington Secretary of State special election|2022]]<ref name=WA2024/>
* Eric Mahaffy (Democratic), blue collar worker and candidate for this district in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington#District 10|2022]]<ref name=WA2024/>
* Nirav Sheth (Republican), restaurant owner<ref name=WA2024/>
